function: No learned PHY function: the DNN only predicts outage probability and ergodic capacity, replacing analysis and Monte Carlo (p. 10); IRS phases use closed-form coherent alignment (p. 18).
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Reason no_learning. The work is a performance analysis (closed-form outage probability, ergodic capacity and throughput over Nakagami-m fading) of a UAV-mounted active/passive IRS NOMA network in which, p. 4: "both the base station and users utilize single-antenna devices". Its only learned component is a supervised multi-output DNN that maps 14 system parameters to OP and ergodic capacity, p. 10: "This section introduces a DNN framework designed to efficiently estimate OP and ergodic capacity", "offering a practical alternative to the demanding nature of mathematical analysis"; p. 4: "we develop a DNN model that offers a high-accuracy, low-latency data-driven alternative for OP and ergodic capacity prediction". No physical-layer decision is learned. The IRS phases are a closed-form coherent alignment, p. 4: "By employing a coherent phase shifting strategy, we derive the optimal signal-to-interference-plus-distortion-plus-noise ratio", and p. 18: "With perfect channel state information, we set the n-th element’s phase shift to" the closed-form value "for optimal channel gain". The NOMA power allocation is a line search, p. 8: "we introduce a straightforward search method to accurately determine the optimal" delta_1 (Algorithm 1). The UAV 3D position, which is above the physical layer anyway, uses p. 8: "an Alternating Optimization (AO) strategy is used" (Algorithm 2). The random-search hyperparameter tuning (p. 11) concerns only the predictor. If the reviewer counts the DNN metric predictor as a learned method, the next code that applies is function, since predicting OP and capacity solves none of the seven areas. The system code would not apply because the link has an IRS.
